title: Nonuniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) versus P/poly
formal: Does \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}=\mathrm{P/poly}\) hold for the nonuniform, single-output Boolean circuit classes defined below? Equivalently, does every polynomial-size bounded-fan-in circuit family have a polynomial-size formula family computing the same functions? This is the opposite polarity of the family-separation question retained as TCS-0019; the two records are consolidated after an individual equivalence review.
why: This is a fundamental comparison between computation with reusable intermediate values and computation with tree structure. Its importance is already represented by the retained active card TCS-0019; keeping both equivalent nonuniform family questions would duplicate the benchmark target.

context_blocks.text: Open Problem 8.3 asks whether every family of functions with polynomial-size circuits also has logarithmic-depth circuits. The early draft’s Chapter 8 is the relevant source location.

Formula balancing and polynomial padding identify this with the negation of the retained linear-circuit versus superpolynomial-formula conjecture. The consolidation preserves the stronger developed formulation, all checked source links and the fact that the two questions have opposite answer polarity.
The previously consolidated Amarilli source asks a broader quantitative improvement question. This review records that distinction instead of attributing an exact class equality to it.

source_consolidations.note: The formula viewpoint asks whether polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits always have polynomial-size formulas. Under the standard AND/OR/NOT basis this is the nonuniform NC¹ versus P/poly frontier, using formula balancing to compare the models.

definitions:
For integers \(n\ge1\), consider total functions \(f_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\). A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph of binary AND and OR gates and unary NOT gates, with variable and constant inputs and one output. Sharing is allowed, and correctness is exact on every input. Circuit size is the number of computational gates; input sources, constants and wires are not counted. Circuit depth counts computational gates on the longest input-to-output path. Constants and literal functions are allowed.

The class \(\mathrm{P/poly}\) consists of families for which one fixed polynomial \(a(n+1)^b\), with positive integers \(a,b\), bounds circuit size at every length. The class \(\mathrm{NC}^{1}\) consists of families with polynomial-size circuits whose depth is at most \(d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) for one fixed positive integer \(d\). The circuits at different lengths need not be generated by an algorithm. All class constants may depend on the family; there is no advice input separate from its choice of circuits, no randomness and no input promise.

A formula is a rooted tree over the same basis, with every occurrence of a variable counted as a separate leaf. Its leaf size counts variable occurrences, including negated ones; constant functions have size zero. Let \(S(f_n)\) and \(L(f_n)\) be minimum circuit gate size and formula leaf size. Formula balancing identifies polynomial formula size with logarithmic circuit depth, and expanding a logarithmic-depth binary circuit into a tree gives the reverse direction.

Thus the exact equality target is: for every family with \(S(f_n)\le a(n+1)^b\) for some fixed \(a,b\), there are fixed \(c,k\) with \(L(f_n)\le c(n+1)^k\) for all \(n\). A negative answer is one polynomial-circuit family violating every polynomial formula bound at arbitrarily large lengths. Padding a family of circuit size \(a(n+1)^b\) to \(a(n+1)^b\) inputs makes its circuit size linear and preserves failure of every polynomial formula bound; the added variables are ignored and other lengths may be assigned constants. Consequently this equality holds if and only if the separation conjecture in TCS-0019 is false.
answer_criterion: A complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof of the equality or its negation would settle the mathematical question. The formulation is preserved here for provenance, but it is no longer a separate active benchmark: an answer has exactly the opposite yes/no polarity from TCS-0019 under the equivalence stated in both records. The editorial consolidation is not a claim that either mathematical answer is known.

review_outcome.reason: The nonuniform class equality is equivalent to the negation of the retained linear-circuit family separation, by formula balancing and polynomial padding.
